text.aura: Your presence is the open ocean: vast, deep and impossible to fully see. Im carries a big, free-spirited, intelligent presence that draws people in like a tide. You read as worldly, curious and slightly unpredictable, the person who just got back from somewhere interesting and is already planning the next thing. Your glow has movement and depth. People sense there's a lot going on under the surface. Your energy can fill a room, but in a relaxed, rolling way rather than a loud one. The glow-up for you isn't being more mysterious. It's adding a sense of anchor, so your expansive energy reads as grounded and trustworthy, not just exciting.
text.how-people-read-you: Before you say a word: interesting, adventurous, a bit hard to pin down. People assume you're well-traveled, open-minded and easygoing, and you usually are. You come across as someone with great stories and big ideas. The misreading: some think you're unreliable or not fully present, because your mind is always moving. Others think you're too cool to care, when you're actually just absorbing everything. You might seem distracted in conversations you're genuinely enjoying. To be read more accurately, show a little consistency. Follow up on what someone told you last time, keep small promises, put your phone face down. Your depth is fascinating. Grounding it makes people trust that the ocean has a shore.
text.colors: Start with your home palette, deep Water: navy, midnight blue, ink, charcoal, black, deep teal. These make you look mysterious, intelligent and effortlessly cool, like a night swim. Metal feeds Water in the five elements, so white, silver and soft gray add clarity and freshness. A navy outfit with silver jewelry is your aura in its best form. For warmth and approachability, add a little Wood: sea green, olive, or a natural linen tone. One structured camel piece gives you shape, but a whole outfit of mustard and brown can make your fluid energy feel stuck. Your colors should feel like the sea at different times of day: deep, shifting and always alive.
text.style: What suits you is effortless cool with a well-traveled edge. Relaxed tailoring, fluid trousers, long coats, oversized shirts, pieces you picked up in different cities. Layers that move suit you, especially in fabrics that drape. You look great in an outfit that could go from a museum to a night out without changing. The trap is looking scattered or careless, too many vibes in one outfit, or so relaxed it reads unbothered rather than cool. Choose a consistent foundation, dark colors and clean shapes, then add one travel-souvenir detail. Hair with natural movement, minimal fuss. Your best photo is near water or in moody evening light, mid-movement, looking toward the horizon.
text.vibe: Your next-level vibe is the anchored adventurer. Picture the free-spirited K-drama character who finally commits to something and becomes even more magnetic because of it. The shift for you is consistency. Show up when you said you would. Finish one project you started. Keep a small ritual, the same café on Sunday mornings, a weekly call with a friend. Let people rely on you. It doesn't cage your freedom. It makes it meaningful. Keep your curiosity, your big questions and your appetite for new places. Just add some depth to the waves. People are drawn to the ocean. They fall in love with the coastline they can return to.
text.aura-dims: The glow goes out when you feel trapped, bored or overwhelmed by too many directions at once. Either you become restless and scattered, starting ten things and finishing none, or you go still and flat, scrolling for hours, uninspired. Your style drifts into whatever's nearest, and you look unfocused. The reset is fresh input with a gentle anchor. Go somewhere you've never been, even if it's a new neighborhood. Spend time near water, a river, a lake, the sea. Read something that expands your mind. Then do one grounding thing: tidy your space, make a simple plan for the week, finish one small task. Oceans need both currents and depth. Give yourself both.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Im, your aura is the ocean. Deep, curious, people get pulled into your orbit.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then you leave mid-conversation because you saw a cool dog.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Navy and silver on you? Mysterious, smart, slightly dangerous. Love it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Your outfit has four countries and three moods in it. Choose.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your glow-up is the anchored adventurer. Freedom plus follow-through.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Show up on time once. People will think you've been replaced.

spring.intro: Spring Wood drinks from Water, so a spring Im aura is a river in flood: generous, adventurous, full of energy flowing outward. Others see you as inspiring and open, the friend who knows a secret beach and will drive you there. Your style can look scattered when your energy is spread across a dozen plans, half festival, half office. Your glow-up is structure. Metal, your resource, brings silver, white and crisp tailoring, which give your flowing energy direction. Keep a deep blue or black base for your Water, and add one fresh green for the season. The spring Im glow is a clear river between stone banks: powerful and beautiful to watch.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Im, half festival, half board meeting. Navy base, silver ring, done. Rivers need banks.

summer.intro: Summer puts Fire in command, and your Water spends itself controlling that heat, so a summer Im aura is the sea in August: sparkling on top, working hard underneath. You come across as relaxed and fun while you are actually keeping everyone's temperature down. Your style can drift into whatever is coolest and easiest to throw on. Your glow-up is replenishment. Metal, your resource, gives white, pearl and silver a central role, and deep ocean blues reinforce your own element. Choose fabrics that move like water: silk, satin, fine cotton. The summer Im glow is a sailing boat on deep blue: crisp white against the sea, fresh and free.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Im, a white silk shirt over ocean blue. You look like a sailing boat.

autumn.intro: Autumn Metal pours into Water, so an autumn Im aura is a river fed by mountain springs: clear, strong and supremely confident. You read as worldly, clever and a little intimidating at parties. You likely look great in black and navy, and you probably own several identical versions of both. The risk is overwhelming people with intensity before they get the chance to know you. Your glow-up is warmth and play. Wood, your output, brings forest green, teal and natural textures, and a touch of Fire softens the cold. Try one unexpected color or a playful accessory. The autumn Im glow is a lake under autumn trees: deep water, warm reflections.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Im, five black jumpers isn't mystery, it's laundry. Try forest green. Let people approach.

winter.intro: Winter doubles your Water, so an Im born then carries the aura of the ocean at its deepest: profound, mysterious and magnetic. People feel pulled toward you but cannot quite read the currents, and some stand at the shore for months. Black, navy and midnight are your natural colors, and in winter you can drown in them. Your glow-up is warmth and direction. Fire brings warmth to a cold sea, so add burgundy, rust or warm gold. Earth gives Water its shape, so a structured camel coat is your power piece. Keep one deep blue item close. The winter Im glow is moonlight on the ocean: vast, and somehow inviting.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Im, a camel coat over midnight blue. Moonlight on the ocean. People come closer.

earth.intro: An Im Water born in the Earth days has the aura of a big river between strong banks: deep, powerful and a bit restrained. People feel your depth and sometimes your pressure. Earth controls Water, so too much brown and khaki can make you look boxed in. Your glow-up is flow with direction. Metal feeds Water, so silver, white and cool gray lift you, and deep blue keeps your own element close. Choose pieces that move: a fluid shirt, a long coat. The Earth-days Im glow is a river running free.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Im, silver and deep blue, in a fabric that flows. River energy. River energy.

strength.strong: A strong Im Water aura is a tide coming in. With plenty of Water and Metal, you seem deep, worldly and magnetic, and your style can feel dark and dramatic: all black, sweeping coats, an air of having just returned from somewhere interesting. The blind spot is overwhelming. People are intrigued but unsure how to start a conversation with you. Add Wood and Earth: forest green, warm camel, natural textures, one playful accessory that makes people smile. Give every look one friendly detail. The ocean is far more inviting when there is a beach to walk on.
strength.weak: A weak Im Water aura is a stream that has lost its course. With little Water or Metal support, you may adopt whatever style is around you, drifting between trends and friends' tastes without ever settling. The blind spot is shrinking into other people's currents until your wardrobe looks like a group chat. Your glow-up is depth and direction: a deep navy coat, a silver ring you never take off, fabrics with real heft. Choose a personal uniform and refine it slowly. A clear channel is what makes your energy look powerful instead of scattered.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood gives your aura lots of drive and upward energy, but it can read as restless or intense, always busy, always growing. Your style may lean practical and outdoorsy, sometimes at the expense of polish. Balance it with Metal touches: a crisp white shirt, silver jewelry, cleaner lines, one tailored piece. Declutter your wardrobe so what remains feels intentional. Your glow is strongest when your ambition looks calm, like a tall tree that doesn't need to prove it's growing.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means your aura can lack a sense of freshness and new beginnings. You might stick to the same outfits for years or feel unsure about trying new styles. Bring in Wood: greens, botanical prints, natural fabrics like linen and cotton, plants in your space. Try one new style element each month, a different silhouette, a new accessory, a new hair clip. Growth looks good on you. Let your style evolve a little, the way spring changes a garden.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your aura bright, bold and sometimes overwhelming. Whether you wear it loudly or quietly, your look can carry more heat than the moment needs: one statement too many, or an intensity people feel before you've said a word. Balance it with Water: navy, deep blue, black accents, calmer silhouettes. Choose one statement per outfit instead of five. Let some quiet into your presence too, listening more, moving slower. Your glow is already strong. Cooling it slightly makes it look richer and more confident.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means your aura can feel understated, sometimes so understated that people overlook you. You might default to neutrals and avoid anything that draws attention. Bring in Fire: a red lip, a coral scarf, warm gold jewelry, a little shimmer. Seek out sunlight in photos and in life. Let yourself be seen in small ways: post the photo, wear the bright thing, laugh openly. Visibility is a skill, and it looks lovely on you when you allow it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth gives you a grounded, warm aura that can slide into heavy or overly practical. Your wardrobe may be comfortable but samey, lots of beige, brown and safe basics. Balance it with Wood: fresh greens, lighter fabrics, a playful print, something that moves when you walk. Try one unexpected piece. Rearrange your space for a fresh feeling. Your stability is beautiful. A little lightness on top keeps it from looking stuck.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth can make your aura feel scattered or ungrounded, lots of ideas, many style moods, not much consistency. Your outfits may change wildly depending on your mood. Bring in Earth: camel, beige, warm brown, ochre, and solid basics like a good coat and reliable shoes. Build a small capsule wardrobe you can trust. Ceramics, wood and warm lighting at home help too. When your foundation is steady, your creativity looks intentional instead of chaotic.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives your aura sharpness and polish that can tip into cold or severe. Your style may be immaculate but a little untouchable: very clean lines, lots of black, white and gray, everything controlled. Balance it with Fire: warm colors near your face, soft textures, a smile that comes sooner. Let one thing be imperfect on purpose, rolled sleeves, tousled hair, a playful accessory. Precision is your strength. Warmth makes it inviting.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal can make your aura feel soft but a little undefined. People like you, but they might not remember your style clearly. Bring in Metal: silver jewelry, crisp white, sharp tailoring, clean shoes, a structured bag. Edit your wardrobe so every piece earns its place. A clear signature, the same ring, the same scent, a consistent color, gives your look definition. Clarity doesn't make you colder. It makes you memorable.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water gives your aura depth and mystery, but it can read as distant, moody or hard to reach. You might hide in dark colors and oversized layers. Balance it with Earth: warm neutrals near your face, structured pieces, a grounded silhouette. Add a little Fire too, a coral or rose accent, to bring warmth. Let people see your expression clearly. Your mystery is magnetic. A bit of warmth makes it feel welcoming, not unreachable.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means your aura can feel busy and bright without much depth or calm. You might always be on, always moving, with little stillness. Bring in Water: navy, midnight blue, black, flowing fabrics, a more relaxed silhouette. Create quiet moments in your day and let them show in your style, softer textures, fewer accessories. Water by your bed and slow evenings help your energy settle. Depth looks good on you. Give it some room.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: hiking boots, three plants and a tote bag. Add one sharp silver thing.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your freshness is gorgeous. A crisp white shirt makes it look intentional.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: red bag, gold chain, leopard coat. Pick one. The others can wait.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your warmth is your magic. Let navy or stone frame it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: beige, oatmeal, sand, more beige. You look like a very calm cupboard.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is beautiful. One silver piece or a deep blue lifts it.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: you look expensive and impossible to talk to. Add one soft texture.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your polish is stunning. A warm knit lets people come closer.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: all black, all mystery, all the time. Even vampires wear burgundy.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is magnetic. A warm color helps people find the door.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Try a sage scarf or a leafy print. Let your style grow a little.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Same outfit since 2021 isn't a signature. It's a rut with good lighting.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? A coral scarf or warm gold earrings changes how people greet you.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: Head-to-toe gray says 'don't notice me'. Is that really the message?

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? A camel coat or a terracotta bag grounds your whole look.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Five trends this month, zero signature. Commit to something longer than a week.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? A crisp white shirt or a silver cuff gives your look clean edges.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Everything slightly creased and slightly oversized reads accidental. Tailor one piece.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? Deep navy or a fluid silk adds calm depth to your look.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Always bright, always on. Let one outfit be quiet. People lean in.
